cleanIntro:
The Taurus RPC is a 9mm Luger roller-delayed blowback pistol built like a small rifle: an upper receiver that hinges off a polymer lower on two takedown pins, a bolt carrier assembly with a rotating bolt head and a separate locking tip, a reversible charging handle, an external manual safety, and a threaded barrel held in the upper by a barrel lock button. Taurus lists two builds, an 8-inch and a 4.5-inch barrel.

The field strip is short: magazine out, bolt locked open twice, rear takedown pin out, upper rotated open, recoil spring support out, bolt carrier assembly out. DEEP CLEAN carries what Taurus publishes beyond that: the bolt carrier assembly apart, the barrel sub-assembly out of the upper, and the magazine apart. Taurus recommends cleaning and lubricating at least every 200 rounds, and after each use.

steps.title: Safety on, finger off, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and push the manual safety all the way up to SAFE. Keep your finger off the trigger and on the indexing pad. Press the magazine release button and take the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: Taurus asks for the safety to be fully up, not halfway. The magazine comes out first so that working the charging handle next cannot feed a fresh round.
steps.quote: 1. Point your firearm in a safe direction and engage the manual safety. 2. Keep your finger off the trigger. 3. Press the magazine release button. 4. Remove the magazine.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Two strokes of the charging handle, then lock it open
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully back at least twice, then engage the bolt catch on the last stroke so the bolt stays open.
steps.prose: Two full strokes give a stuck case two chances to be extracted and thrown clear. Watch the ejection port as you do it: a round that comes out is the reason for the step.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle, performing at least two safety strokes, and engage the bolt catch so that it remains in the open position.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Look and feel — chamber and magazine well
steps.action: With the bolt locked open, look into the chamber and the magazine well, and feel both with a fingertip. Only when both are empty, close the bolt — either with the bolt catch, or by pulling the charging handle fully back and letting it go.
steps.prose: Seeing is not enough on its own; Taurus asks for both a visual and a physical check.
steps.quote: With the bolt open, visually and physically ensure the chamber and magazine well are empty.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28
steps.warn: NEVER ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE OR CLEAN A LOADED FIREARM. DOING SO CAN RESULT IN SERIOUS BODILY INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out
steps.action: With your thumb, push the rear takedown pin until it clicks; a pin punch can help start it. Then pull it from the other side until it stops at its full travel.
steps.prose: The pin stays in the lower at the end of its travel. With it out, the rear of the upper is free.
steps.quote: 7. Using your thumb, push the rear takedown pin until you hear a click. A pin punch may be used to assist with this operation. Then, pull the pin from the other side until it reaches its full travel.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Rotate the upper open
steps.action: Rotate the upper receiver up and away from the lower to open the gun.
steps.prose: This exposes the mechanism housing, the bolt assembly and the bolt carrier.
steps.quote:
Rotate the upper receiver as shown in Figure 4 to access the
mechanism housing, bolt assembly, and bolt carrier.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Recoil spring support out
steps.action: Gently press the lower part of the recoil spring support to free it from the receiver latch, and at the same time pull it out of the gun.
steps.prose: The support sits at the rear of the recoil spring assembly and locks into the receiver. Press and pull together; pulling alone will not free it.
steps.quote: 9. Gently press the lower part of the support so that it is released from the receiver latch, while simultaneously pulling it out of the weapon.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Bolt carrier assembly out
steps.action: Tilt the gun level to get at the receiver, and push the bolt carrier assembly out.
steps.prose: The bolt carrier assembly carries the bolt head, the locking tip and the firing pin; it comes out in one piece here.
steps.quote: 10. Tilt the weapon horizontally to access the lower receiver. Push the bolt carrier assembly out of the receiver.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the lower with the upper rotated open, the recoil spring assembly, the bolt carrier assembly and the magazine. This is Taurus's first-level disassembly. DEEP CLEAN carries what the book publishes beyond it: the bolt carrier assembly apart, the barrel out of the upper, and the magazine apart.
steps.prose: Taurus calls this the disassembly needed for routine maintenance.
steps.quote: For the maintenance of your Taurus firearm, it is necessary to perform a first-level disassembly.
steps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — First-Step Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Bolt head off the carrier
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt head back against the bolt carrier, rotate it 90 degrees counterclockwise to release it, then pull it forward off the assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Push, turn, pull — in that order. It will not turn until it is pushed home against the carrier.
deepSteps.quote: With the bolt assembly removed from the upper receiver, push the bolt head against the bolt carrier, rotate the head 90 degrees counterclockwise to release it from the bolt carrier. Then pull the bolt head forward to detach it from the assembly.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Bolt Carrier Assembly, printed p.30

deepSteps.title: Locking tip, firing pin and spring out
deepSteps.action: Take the locking tip out of the carrier with the firing pin and spring still in it, then take the firing pin and spring out of the locking tip.
deepSteps.prose: The RPC ships with a 110-degree locking tip for standard ammunition and an 85-degree tip in the box for subsonic or suppressed use. Note which one is in your gun so the same one goes back.
deepSteps.caution: Use of the correct locking tip is critical to ensure proper function and safe operation of the firearm.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Remove the locking tip together with the firing pin and spring. 3. Remove the firing pin and spring from inside the locking tip.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Bolt Carrier Assembly, printed p.30

deepSteps.title: Front takedown pin out, handguard off
deepSteps.action: To take the barrel out, Taurus sends you back to the handguard steps. With your thumb, push the front takedown pin from the left side until it clicks (a pin punch can help), then pull it from the right side to its full travel. Pull the handguard firmly forward out of its housing in the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The book's barrel procedure opens by repeating these steps from its charging-handle section.
deepSteps.quote: Repeat the disassembly steps, as previously described on page 20.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Barrel Sub-Assembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: Barrel lock button to unlocked
deepSteps.action: Press the barrel lock button at the front until its tip lifts above the housing. Holding it down, put a 5 mm hex key in it and turn it 180 degrees clockwise, until the button points to unlocked and rests in the opposite slot.
deepSteps.prose: Half a turn, clockwise. The button must sit fully in the unlocked slot before the barrel will pull free.
deepSteps.quote: Press the barrel lock button in the front area until the tip lifts above the housing. While holding the lock button down (Figure 4), insert a 5mm hex key, turn it 180 degrees clockwise until the button points to the "unlocked" position (Figure 6), and rests in the opposite slot (unlocked).
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Barrel Sub-Assembly, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Barrel sub-assembly out
deepSteps.action: Hold the receiver firmly and pull the barrel sub-assembly hard out of its housing until it is completely free.
deepSteps.prose: It takes a firm pull. Clean the barrel and the inside of the upper before it goes back.
deepSteps.quote: 4. While firmly holding the receiver, pull the Barrel Sub-Assembly strongly out of its housing until it is completely free.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Barrel Sub-Assembly, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart
deepSteps.action: Press the base plate lock on the magazine and, keeping it pressed, slide the base plate off. Then take out the magazine spring, the follower and the spring base.
deepSteps.prose: Keep a thumb over the bottom of the magazine as the plate comes off. Note which way the follower faces so it goes back the same way.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Press the magazine base plate lock. While keeping it pressed, slide the base plate in the direction shown until it is completely removed. 2. Remove the magazine spring, follower, and spring base.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Disassembly of the Magazine, printed p.30
deepSteps.warn: When removing the base plate, be careful with the internal parts that are under spring tension, as they may eject suddenly and forcefully from the magazine.

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly
deepSteps.action: Stop here. The trigger group, the hammer, the extractor, the locking rollers and everything else in the exploded view stay as they are.
deepSteps.prose: This is where Taurus's published disassembly ends.
deepSteps.quote: Disassembly of the firearm beyond these steps is not recommended unless performed by a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite:
TAURUS
RPC
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 1 — Assembly, printed p.32

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent to take off the firing residue
Run a dry cotton patch through the bore to take out the remaining residue and solvent
Dry the inside of the barrel and chamber after cleaning
Deep clean: with the barrel out, clean the barrel and the inside of the upper receiver free of debris and put a light amount of oil around the barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Brush the bolt free of debris
Brush the bolt face and the area under the extractor claw until they are completely clean
A small drop of good gun oil on each side surface of the bolt and on the rails

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Wipe the outside of the frame with a soft cloth
Clean the internal parts with a soft brush; firearm solvent may be used, then removed completely so the frame is dry and clean
Lubricate the frame rails and the barrel lockup points
Check for loose screws or pins; tighten the screws and press the pins back in as needed

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the magazine with a soft brush when it needs it
Wipe the spring and the follower with a clean cloth
Do not use solvents on polymer magazines
Any solvent used on the metal parts comes off completely before reassembly, so it cannot contaminate the ammunition

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the outside with a non-abrasive cloth and brush dust and residue out of the small crevices
After cleaning, rub the gun over with a lightly oiled cloth
Never clean a gun with a laser fitted in a machine that submerges it

reassembly: Deep clean only: magazine spring base, spring and follower back into the body, and the base plate slid back on until its lock catches.

Deep clean only: barrel sub-assembly back in, the reverse of how it came out. Make sure the barrel is seated all the way back so the barrel lock button can rotate freely under it and lock it; then the handguard back on and the front takedown pin pushed home.
Deep clean only: spring into the firing pin, and both into the locking tip.
Deep clean only: locking tip, with its firing pin and spring, into the bolt carrier, lined up with the shape of the slot.
Deep clean only: bolt head onto the locking tip, pushed to the end of its travel, then turned 90 degrees clockwise until the bolt carrier assembly is fully joined.
Bolt carrier assembly into the receiver housing, pushed fully into position.
Recoil spring assembly into the hole in the bolt carrier, pushed until the recoil spring support at the rear locks into the receiver.
Upper rotated back down into the lower, and the rear takedown pin pushed in until it locks.
Cycle the bolt carrier assembly two or three times to check it went together correctly.
fncheck: With no magazine and the chamber empty, cycle the bolt carrier assembly two or three times with the charging handle: it should run fully back and return fully forward under its spring every time. Push the manual safety all the way up to SAFE and back down to FIRE, and check it stops fully in each position. If you changed the locking tip, make sure the one installed matches the ammunition you will shoot — 110 degree for standard ammunition, 85 degree for subsonic or suppressed. Then take the gun back to the clear check before loading.
